title: Introduction to pointers
recap: A pointer stores an address. The address-of operator obtains an object's address, while indirection accesses the object at a valid pointed-to address.
Changing a value through a pointer differs from changing which address the local pointer stores. Pointers do not own an object merely because they point to it.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement doublePointed(value), doubling the caller's integer through a pointer. For this lesson the pointer is guaranteed non-null and the product fits int. Use indirection to access the pointed-to object rather than modifying the local pointer value.
hints: Multiply the pointed-to integer, not an address.
No allocation or deletion is needed.
